name: Skill Move Set
description: Named dribble moves — stepover, feint, spin — as committed animations with a risk/reward roll, not free-floating style. Each move locks the carrier for its duration and pits the mover's controlRating against the defender's reaction: success emits movement.defenderBeaten, failure risks movement.ballLoose, and the same roll decides both so a move can never be safe AND brilliant. It layers on movement.ball_carrier rather than replacing basic dribbling, because skill moves are exceptions to control and exceptions should pay for their spotlight. Which moves a player owns is per-entity data, so a youth-academy fullback and a star winger legitimately carry different sets — the set is progression surface, not a global unlock list.

inputs.name: moveSet
inputs.description: Moves this entity may attempt, by name against the shared move table. The default trio covers the three risk tiers; anything fancier is earned per-player, which is what keeps move-spam from being the meta.

inputs.name: commitLockSeconds
inputs.description: Input lockout while a move animates. The lock is the price of the move — cancelling mid-animation would let players sample the roll and bail, which converts risk/reward into pure reward.

inputs.name: successBonus
inputs.description: Flat bonus added to the mover's controlRating for the roll. Small on purpose: a move should tilt the odds, not replace the stat — otherwise the move name matters more than the player using it.

inputs.name: failureLooseChance
inputs.description: Probability a failed move spills the ball loose instead of merely failing in place. Half by default: failure must sometimes be recoverable, or attempting a move inside your own half becomes strictly irrational.

inputs.name: staminaCostPerMove
inputs.description: Stamina charged per attempt, success or fail. The cost is what stops move-chains from being free; it reads whoever owns stamina (combat.vital_stats in survival crossovers, a match stat here) rather than keeping a private battery.

outputs.name: activeMove
outputs.description: Name of the move currently animating, empty when idle. Animation and camera layers read this; gameplay systems should read the outcome events instead.

outputs.name: isCommitted
outputs.description: True during the lock window. movement.ball_carrier consults this before accepting a pass or shoot input, so a committed player cannot accidentally pass mid-stepover.
